correctness.rationale: The exact rational commutator equality was independently reproduced from f_i and f_i prime; the scalar-flow comparison is proved by differentiating the phase map and applying scalar comparison, then bubble-sort exchanges minimize all permutations. For r>Rstar, a strictly reversed bracket and the second-order small-time flow expansion prove sharp failure. The quadratic supremum formula handles all coefficient signs. Standard-library verification passed 1,500 exact rational identity checks and 6,558 sign checks, plus exact examples and 25 numerical permutation cases. The proof establishes the infinite statement; these finite checks supplement it.

originality.rationale: Actual published-record queries for serial Holling-II predation and scalar-flow ordering found no exact statement among the returned results. Three highly relevant accessible primary works were examined in full HTML; their objects are functional-response inference, trophic-cascade forcing, and periodic impulsive-system stability, not an all-density/all-duration sharp serial-treatment ordering threshold. One particularly plausible 2005 multipredator paper remained inaccessible in full text, and broader scalar-flow comparison theorems are a material residual implication risk. The exact quadratic phase threshold is differentiated from the general flow-comparison lemma used to prove it; no priority or exhaustive uniqueness is asserted.
residual_risks: Full text of Pei et al. (2005) was inaccessible; the available abstract cannot decide exact implication coverage.
A more general published one-dimensional flow rearrangement or switching-control theorem might supply stronger coverage; the scalar comparison lemma itself is standard.
The model assumes constant predator density in each phase, and finite ecological applicability is not empirically verified.

value.rationale: This is an exact all-density, all-duration scheduling classification for finite serial predator treatments, with an analytically sharp boundary rstar computable solely from quadratic maxima. It distinguishes universal ecological planning from regime-dependent scheduling and exhibits a genuine sign reversal despite both phases reducing prey. The physical question and exact threshold are independently motivated; the finding is not offered as a novel general flow comparison principle.
